title.en: Present Perfect or Past Simple? (I saw / I have seen)
title.es: ¿Presente perfecto o pasado simple? (I saw / I have seen)

text.en: Mexican Spanish often uses the simple past where English uses the present perfect: “Ya comí”, “Hoy fui al banco”. English separates two things: when there is a finished time (yesterday, last year, in 2015, two days ago) you need the past simple: “I saw him yesterday”. When there is no time, or the time lasts up to now and the thing is connected to the present, you need the present perfect: “I have seen that movie”, “I have lived here since 2020”.
text.es: El español de México usa muchas veces el pretérito donde el inglés usa el presente perfecto: «Ya comí», «Hoy fui al banco». El inglés separa dos cosas: si hay un momento terminado (yesterday, last year, in 2015, two days ago) hace falta el pasado simple: «I saw him yesterday». Si no hay un momento, o el tiempo llega hasta ahora y el hecho tiene relación con el presente, hace falta el presente perfecto: «I have seen that movie», «I have lived here since 2020».

title.en: Irregular verbs: past simple and past participle
title.es: Verbos irregulares: pasado simple y participio

text.en: A finished time: yesterday, last week, in 2015, two days ago, when I was ten. The time is in the sentence or in the conversation, so it is not the present perfect.
text.es: Un momento terminado: yesterday, last week, in 2015, two days ago, when I was ten. El momento está en la oración o en la conversación, por eso no es presente perfecto.

tr.en: I saw him yesterday.
tr.es: Lo vi ayer.

examples.es: We went to Mexico last year.

tr.en: We went to Mexico last year.
tr.es: Fuimos a México el año pasado.

text.en: A question about a finished moment: When…? What time…? Where were you…? These questions take the past simple (did + base verb, or was / were), never the present perfect.
text.es: Pregunta sobre un momento terminado: When…? What time…? Where were you…? Estas preguntas llevan pasado simple (did + verbo base, o was / were), nunca presente perfecto.

tr.en: When did you arrive?
tr.es: ¿Cuándo llegaste?

examples.es: What time did the movie start?

tr.en: What time did the movie start?
tr.es: ¿A qué hora empezó la película?

text.en: A period that is over: something happened long ago and it does not continue. The focus is on the past, with no link to the present.
text.es: Un periodo terminado: algo pasó hace tiempo y ya no continúa. El foco está en el pasado, sin relación con el presente.

examples.es: My brother lived in Spain for two years.

tr.en: My brother lived in Spain for two years.
tr.es: Mi hermano vivió dos años en España.

examples.es: She worked there until last year.

tr.en: She worked there until last year.
tr.es: Trabajó allí hasta el año pasado.

title.en: Present perfect: a link to now
title.es: Presente perfecto: una conexión con ahora

text.en: Experience with no time: ever (in questions), never, before. What matters is whether it ever happened, not when.
text.es: Experiencia sin decir cuándo: ever (en preguntas), never, before. Importa si pasó alguna vez, no cuándo.

examples.es: Have you ever been to Oaxaca?

tr.en: Have you ever been to Oaxaca?
tr.es: ¿Has estado alguna vez en Oaxaca?

examples.es: I have never been to Peru.

tr.en: I have never been to Peru.
tr.es: Nunca he estado en Perú.

text.en: Time up to now: for + a duration (for five years), since + a starting point (since 2020), How long…? The period is not over yet.
text.es: Tiempo hasta ahora: for + una duración (for five years), since + un punto de inicio (since 2020), How long…? El periodo todavía no termina.

examples.es: I have lived here for five years.

tr.en: I have lived here for five years.
tr.es: Vivo aquí desde hace cinco años.

examples.es: How long have you studied English?

tr.en: How long have you studied English?
tr.es: ¿Desde cuándo estudias inglés?

text.en: Recent news or a result: just, already, yet, so far. The action still matters now. In casual American speech you also hear the past simple here, but in writing and on exams use the present perfect.
text.es: Noticia reciente o resultado: just, already, yet, so far. La acción todavía importa ahora. En el habla informal de Estados Unidos aquí también se oye el pasado simple, pero por escrito y en exámenes usa el presente perfecto.

examples.es: I have just finished my homework.

tr.en: I have just finished my homework.
tr.es: Acabo de terminar mi tarea.

tr.en: Have you eaten yet?
tr.es: ¿Ya comiste?

text.en: Don’t translate the tense of your Spanish sentence. Ask yourself: is there a finished time (yesterday, last year, two days ago)? Then use the past simple. No time, or time that lasts up to now? Then use the present perfect.
text.es: No traduzcas el tiempo de tu oración en español. Pregúntate: ¿hay un momento terminado (ayer, el año pasado, hace dos días)? Entonces pasado simple. ¿No hay momento, o el tiempo llega hasta ahora? Entonces presente perfecto.

text.en: “Vivo aquí desde 2020” is not “I live here since 2020” in English, it is “I have lived here since 2020”. For time that lasts up to now, for and since go with the present perfect.
text.es: «Vivo aquí desde 2020» no es «I live here since 2020» en inglés, sino «I have lived here since 2020». Para el tiempo que llega hasta ahora, for y since van con el presente perfecto.

text.en: A When…? question asks about a finished time, so it does not take the present perfect. Not “When have you arrived?” but “When did you arrive?”.
text.es: Una pregunta con When…? pide un momento terminado, por eso no lleva presente perfecto. No «When have you arrived?», sino «When did you arrive?».

text.en: Two different participles: “She has gone to the market” (she went and is still there), “She has been to the market” (she went and came back). After have the past simple form never appears: not “I have went”, but “I have gone”.
text.es: Dos participios distintos: «She has gone to the market» (se fue y sigue allí), «She has been to the market» (fue y ya volvió). Después de have nunca va la forma del pasado simple: no «I have went», sino «I have gone».

speak.en: When there is a finished time, such as «yesterday», «last week» or «two days ago», you need the past simple: «I saw him yesterday». When there is no time, or the time lasts up to now, you need the present perfect: «I have seen that movie», «I have lived here since May». After «for» comes a duration, after «since» a starting point. A «when» question asks about a finished time, so: «When did you arrive?». Careful: not «I have seen him yesterday», and not «I live here since May». «Gone» and «been» are different: «She has gone to the market» means she is still there.
speak.es: Si hay un momento terminado, por ejemplo «yesterday», «last week» o «two days ago», hace falta el pasado simple: «I saw him yesterday». Si no hay un momento, o el tiempo llega hasta ahora, hace falta el presente perfecto: «I have seen that movie», «I have lived here since May». Con «for» va una duración y con «since» un punto de inicio. Una pregunta con «when» pide un momento terminado, entonces: «When did you arrive?». Cuidado: no «I have seen him yesterday», y no «I live here since May». «Gone» y «been» son distintos: «She has gone to the market» significa que sigue allí.

items.sentence: We ___ a good movie last night.

why.en: “Last night” is a finished time, so you need the past simple: We saw a good movie last night.
why.es: «Last night» es un momento terminado, así que hace falta el pasado simple: We saw a good movie last night.

have seen.en: You don’t use the present perfect with a finished time (“last night”); you need the past simple (saw).
have seen.es: Con un momento terminado («last night») no se usa el presente perfecto; hace falta el pasado simple (saw).

see.en: “See” is present, but “last night” points to the past; you need the past simple: saw.
see.es: «See» es presente, pero «last night» habla del pasado; hace falta el pasado simple: saw.

tr.en: We saw a good movie last night.
tr.es: Vimos una buena película anoche.

why.en: “In 2015” is a finished time, so you need the past simple: lived.
why.es: «In 2015» es un momento terminado, así que hace falta el pasado simple: lived.

has lived.en: The present perfect does not go with a finished year (“in 2015”); you need the past simple.
has lived.es: El presente perfecto no va con un año terminado («in 2015»); hace falta el pasado simple.

lives.en: “Lives” is present, but the year 2015 points to the past; you need the past simple: lived.
lives.es: «Lives» es presente, pero el año 2015 habla del pasado; hace falta el pasado simple: lived.

tr.en: My sister lived in Guadalajara in 2015.
tr.es: Mi hermana vivió en Guadalajara en el 2015.

items.sentence: You live in Mexico now. When ___ you arrive here?

why.en: A When question asks about a finished time, so you need the past simple: did + base verb (When did you arrive?).
why.es: Una pregunta con When pide un momento terminado, así que hace falta el pasado simple: did + verbo base (When did you arrive?).

do.en: “Do” makes a present question, but the arrival already happened; the past needs did.
do.es: «Do» forma una pregunta en presente, pero la llegada ya pasó; para el pasado hace falta did.

have.en: You don’t use the present perfect with a When question (not “When have you arrived?”); you need did.
have.es: Con una pregunta con When no se usa el presente perfecto (no «When have you arrived?»); hace falta did.

tr.en: You live in Mexico now. When did you arrive here?
tr.es: Vives en México ahora. ¿Cuándo llegaste aquí?

items.sentence: She has studied English ___ three years.

why.en: Three years is a duration, and with the present perfect a duration takes for: for three years.
why.es: Tres años es una duración, y con el presente perfecto una duración lleva for: for three years.

ago.en: “Ago” gives a past point in time with the past simple (three years ago), not a duration after has studied.
ago.es: «Ago» da un punto en el pasado con el pasado simple (three years ago), no una duración después de has studied.

since.en: Since needs a starting point (since 2021), not a duration; “three years” is a duration, so you need for.
since.es: Since pide un punto de inicio (since 2021), no una duración; «three years» es una duración, por eso hace falta for.

examples: I have worked here for two years.
He has lived here for ten years.

tr.en: She has studied English for three years.
tr.es: Ella estudió inglés por tres años.

why.en: “Monday” is a starting point, so you need since: since Monday.
why.es: «Monday» es un punto de inicio, así que hace falta since: since Monday.

for.en: For goes before a duration (for three days); “Monday” is not a duration but a starting point.
for.es: For va antes de una duración (for three days); «Monday» no es una duración sino un punto de inicio.

ago.en: “Ago” follows a duration (three days ago) and goes with the past simple; here the verb is in the present perfect.
ago.es: «Ago» va después de una duración (three days ago) y con el pasado simple; aquí el verbo está en presente perfecto.

examples: She has lived here since May.
They have been here since last week.

tr.en: I haven't seen him since Monday.
tr.es: No lo he visto desde el lunes.

why.en: In a question, the word for “already” is yet: Have you finished the project yet?
why.es: En una pregunta, la palabra para «ya» es yet: Have you finished the project yet?

yesterday.en: “Yesterday” is a finished time and needs the past simple (Did you finish…?), not the present perfect.
yesterday.es: «Yesterday» es un momento terminado y pide el pasado simple (Did you finish…?), no el presente perfecto.

ago.en: “Ago” gives a past point in time with the past simple; it does not fit a Have you finished… question.
ago.es: «Ago» da un punto en el pasado con el pasado simple; no encaja con una pregunta Have you finished….

tr.en: Have you finished the project yet?
tr.es: ¿Ya terminaste el proyecto?

why.en: An experience with no time: Have you ever been…? (have + been, the present perfect).
why.es: Una experiencia sin decir cuándo: Have you ever been…? (have + been, presente perfecto).

Did.en: After did you need the base verb (Did you ever go…?); “been” is a participle, so did does not fit.
Did.es: Después de did hace falta el verbo base (Did you ever go…?); «been» es un participio, por eso did no encaja.

Were.en: “Were been” is not a possible form; “been” comes after have: Have you ever been…?
Were.es: «Were been» no es una forma posible; «been» va después de have: Have you ever been…?

examples: Have you ever seen this movie?

tr.en: Have you ever been to Oaxaca?
tr.es: ¿Alguna vez has estado en Oaxaca?

items.sentence: How long ___ you lived in Mexico?

why.en: A “how long” question asks about a period that lasts up to now: How long have you lived…? (present perfect).
why.es: Una pregunta «how long» pregunta por un periodo que llega hasta ahora: How long have you lived…? (presente perfecto).

did.en: “Lived” is already a past form; after did you would need the base verb (How long did you live…?), but time up to now asks for the present perfect.
did.es: «Lived» ya es una forma de pasado; después de did haría falta el verbo base (How long did you live…?), pero el tiempo hasta ahora pide presente perfecto.

do.en: After do you need the base verb, but “lived” is a past form; the sentence would be wrong. Have lived is the right structure.
do.es: Después de do hace falta el verbo base, pero «lived» es una forma de pasado; la oración sería incorrecta. Have lived es la estructura correcta.

examples: How long have you worked here?
How long has she lived here?

tr.en: How long have you lived in Mexico?
tr.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo has vivido en México?

items.sentence: He ___ his leg when he was ten.

why.en: “When he was ten” is a finished time, so you need the past simple: broke.
why.es: «When he was ten» es un momento terminado, así que hace falta el pasado simple: broke.

has broken.en: The present perfect cannot be used when the sentence says when it happened (“when he was ten”).
has broken.es: El presente perfecto no se puede usar cuando la oración dice cuándo pasó («when he was ten»).

breaks.en: “Breaks” is present; the break happened long ago, so you need the past simple: broke.
breaks.es: «Breaks» es presente; la fractura pasó hace tiempo, así que hace falta el pasado simple: broke.

examples: She broke her phone last week.

tr.en: He broke his leg when he was ten.
tr.es: Él se rompió la pierna cuando tenía diez años.

items.sentence: Ana has ___ to the market. She will be back soon.

why.en: Ana went and is not back yet (she will be back soon): has gone. Has been would mean she already came back.
why.es: Ana se fue y todavía no regresa (volverá pronto): has gone. Has been significaría que ya volvió.

been.en: Has been means she went and came back; Ana is still away, so you need gone.
been.es: Has been significa que fue y ya volvió; Ana todavía no está aquí, por eso hace falta gone.

went.en: After has comes the participle, not the past simple form (not “has went”).
went.es: Después de has va el participio, no la forma del pasado simple (no «has went»).

tr.en: Ana has gone to the market. She will be back soon.
tr.es: Ana se fue al mercado. Regresará pronto.

items.sentence: Look at the window! Someone has ___ it.

why.en: After has you need the participle: has broken.
why.es: Después de has hace falta el participio: has broken.

broke.en: “Broke” is the past simple form; after has/have comes the participle (broken).
broke.es: «Broke» es la forma del pasado simple; después de has/have va el participio (broken).

break.en: “Break” is the base verb; after has you need the participle (broken), not the base verb.
break.es: «Break» es el verbo base; después de has hace falta el participio (broken), no el verbo base.

tr.en: Look at the window! Someone has broken it.
tr.es: ¡Mira la ventana! Alguien la rompió.

why.en: After have never you need the participle: I have never been to Peru.
why.es: Después de have never hace falta el participio: I have never been to Peru.

went.en: “Went” is the past simple; after have comes the participle (been). Not “I have never went”.
went.es: «Went» es el pasado simple; después de have va el participio (been). No «I have never went».

go.en: “Go” is the base verb; after have you need a participle. “Been to” is the form that means “I have visited”.
go.es: «Go» es el verbo base; después de have hace falta un participio. «Been to» es la forma que significa «he estado allí».

examples: She has never been to Madrid.

tr.en: I have never been to Peru.
tr.es: Nunca he estado en Perú.

items.sentence: Did you see Carlos at the party? Yes, I ___ him there.

why.en: The question is about a finished event (the party), so the answer is also the past simple: I saw him there.
why.es: La pregunta es sobre un evento terminado (la fiesta), por eso la respuesta también va en pasado simple: I saw him there.

have seen.en: The question is in the past simple (Did you see…?) and the party is a finished event; the answer is also the past simple.
have seen.es: La pregunta está en pasado simple (Did you see…?) y la fiesta es un evento terminado; la respuesta también va en pasado simple.

see.en: “See” is present, but the party already happened; you need the past simple: saw.
see.es: «See» es presente, pero la fiesta ya pasó; hace falta el pasado simple: saw.

tr.en: Did you see Carlos at the party? Yes, I saw him there.
tr.es: ¿Viste a Carlos en la fiesta? Sí, lo vi ahí.

items.sentence: Ana ___ in Madrid for two years, but now she lives here.

why.en: The years in Madrid are over (now she lives here), so you need the past simple: lived.
why.es: Los años en Madrid terminaron (ahora vive aquí), así que hace falta el pasado simple: lived.

has lived.en: Has lived would mean she still lives there; the second half (now she lives here) says the opposite.
has lived.es: Has lived significaría que todavía vive allí; la segunda parte (now she lives here) dice lo contrario.

lives.en: “Lives” is present, but the years in Madrid belong to the past; you need the past simple.
lives.es: «Lives» es presente, pero los años en Madrid son del pasado; hace falta el pasado simple.

examples: She worked there for a year.
They lived there for six months.

tr.en: Ana lived in Madrid for two years, but now she lives here.
tr.es: Ana vivió en Madrid por dos años, pero ahora vive aquí.

items.sentence: Ana has lived in Puebla ___ she was a child.

why.en: “She was a child” is a starting point, not a duration, so you need since: since she was a child.
why.es: «She was a child» es un punto de inicio, no una duración, así que hace falta since: since she was a child.

for.en: For needs a duration (for ten years); “she was a child” gives a starting point.
for.es: For pide una duración (for ten years); «she was a child» da un punto de inicio.

ago.en: “Ago” follows a duration and goes with the past simple (ten years ago); it does not fit this sentence.
ago.es: «Ago» va después de una duración y con el pasado simple (ten years ago); no encaja en esta oración.

examples: We have been friends since school.
I have been here since May.

tr.en: Ana has lived in Puebla since she was a child.
tr.es: Ana ha vivido en Puebla desde que era niña.

items.sentence: This is the best food I have ever ___.

why.en: After have ever you need the participle: I have ever eaten. A superlative with ever takes the present perfect.
why.es: Después de have ever hace falta el participio: I have ever eaten. Un superlativo con ever lleva presente perfecto.

ate.en: “Ate” is the past simple; after have ever comes the participle (eaten).
ate.es: «Ate» es el pasado simple; después de have ever va el participio (eaten).

eat.en: “Eat” is the base verb; after have you need the participle (eaten).
eat.es: «Eat» es el verbo base; después de have hace falta el participio (eaten).

examples: This is the best movie I have ever seen.
He is the best friend I have ever had.

tr.en: This is the best food I have ever eaten.
tr.es: Esta es la mejor comida que he comido en mi vida.

items.sentence: They moved to Puebla two years ___.

why.en: A duration + ago gives a past point in time with the past simple: two years ago.
why.es: Una duración + ago da un punto en el pasado con el pasado simple: two years ago.

since.en: Since goes before a starting point (since 2023) and takes the present perfect; here “moved” is the past simple.
since.es: Since va antes de un punto de inicio (since 2023) y lleva presente perfecto; aquí «moved» es pasado simple.

for.en: For goes before a duration and takes the present perfect (for two years). Here the blank comes after the duration, and that is where ago fits.
for.es: For va antes de una duración y lleva presente perfecto (for two years). Aquí el hueco va después de la duración, y ahí encaja ago.

tr.en: They moved to Puebla two years ago.
tr.es: Ellos se mudaron a Puebla hace dos años.

items.sentence: It's only Wednesday. I ___ four meetings this week so far.

why.en: “So far” shows that the week is still going, so you need the present perfect: have had.
why.es: «So far» indica que la semana todavía sigue, así que hace falta el presente perfecto: have had.

had.en: The past simple points to a finished time; “so far” says the week is not over, so you need the present perfect.
had.es: El pasado simple apunta a un tiempo terminado; «so far» dice que la semana no ha terminado, por eso hace falta el presente perfecto.

was having.en: “Was having” describes a process in the past; “so far” asks for a total up to now (have had).
was having.es: «Was having» describe un proceso en el pasado; «so far» pide un total hasta ahora (have had).

examples: I have read two books this month.
She has called me three times today.

tr.en: It's only Wednesday. I have had four meetings this week so far.
tr.es: Apenas es miércoles. He tenido cuatro juntas en lo que va de la semana.

tr.en: I have never eaten fish.
tr.es: Nunca he comido pescado.

text.en: past simple: with a finished time
text.es: pasado simple: con un tiempo terminado

wrong.en: The sentence has no finished time (yesterday, last year); “never” is an experience of a whole life, so the present perfect is used.
wrong.es: La oración no tiene un momento terminado (yesterday, last year); «never» es una experiencia de toda la vida, por eso se usa el presente perfecto.

text.en: present simple: a habit
text.es: presente simple: un hábito

wrong.en: A habit would be “I never eat fish”. “Have eaten” uses a participle, so this is not the present simple.
wrong.es: Un hábito sería «I never eat fish». «Have eaten» lleva participio, así que no es presente simple.

text.en: present perfect: an experience with no time given
text.es: presente perfecto: una experiencia sin decir cuándo

tr.en: She moved to Mexico in 2019.
tr.es: Ella se mudó a México en 2019.

text.en: past simple: a finished time (in 2019)
text.es: pasado simple: un tiempo terminado (en 2019)

text.en: present perfect: an experience
text.es: presente perfecto: una experiencia

wrong.en: “In 2019” says when it happened, so it is not the present perfect but the past simple.
wrong.es: «In 2019» dice cuándo pasó, por eso no es presente perfecto sino pasado simple.

text.en: present simple: a situation now
text.es: presente simple: una situación ahora

wrong.en: “Moved” is a past form, and “in 2019” points to the past; this does not describe a situation now.
wrong.es: «Moved» es una forma de pasado y «in 2019» habla del pasado; esto no describe una situación ahora.

items.es: We have lived here for five years.

tr.en: We have lived here for five years.
tr.es: Vivimos aquí desde hace cinco años.

text.en: past simple: a period that is over
text.es: pasado simple: un periodo terminado

wrong.en: The past simple would mean they no longer live there; have lived and for show that the period still lasts.
wrong.es: El pasado simple significaría que ya no viven allí; have lived y for muestran que el periodo todavía continúa.

text.en: present simple: a situation now
text.es: presente simple: una situación ahora

wrong.en: Spanish uses the present (“vivimos desde hace cinco años”), but in English for + a duration needs the present perfect.
wrong.es: El español usa el presente («vivimos desde hace cinco años»), pero en inglés for + una duración necesita presente perfecto.

text.en: present perfect: time up to now
text.es: presente perfecto: el tiempo hasta ahora

items.es: When did you buy this car?

tr.en: When did you buy this car?
tr.es: ¿Cuándo compraste este carro?

text.en: present perfect: have + participle
text.es: presente perfecto: have + participio

wrong.en: A When question asks about a finished time, so not “When have you bought…?” but did + base verb.
wrong.es: Una pregunta con When pide un momento terminado, por eso no «When have you bought…?» sino did + verbo base.

text.en: past simple: When asks about a finished time
text.es: pasado simple: When pide un momento terminado

text.en: present simple: a habit
text.es: presente simple: un hábito

wrong.en: Did is the helper verb of the past tense; the purchase happened once, it is not a habit.
wrong.es: Did es el verbo auxiliar del pasado; la compra pasó una vez, no es un hábito.

pairs.en: I have already finished the project.

pairs.es: Hace dos días llamé a mi mamá.
pairs.en: I called my mom two days ago.
